evidence.quote: IMP1: ALLO-501A, an allogeneic CAR T targeting CD19.
ALLO-501A is an allogeneic TRAC/CD52-knockout chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T cell therapy targeting CD19.
ALLO-501A is engineered using a self-inactivating lentiviral vector (LVV), which drives expression of a second-generation CAR, thus redirecting T cells to target CD19.

construct utilized in ALLO-501A combines a single-chain variable fragment (scFv) derived from a murine anti-human CD19 monoclonal antibody, with the human CD8 hinge and transmembrane domains, and a cytoplasmic tail composed of human 4-1BB co-stimulatory and human CD3ζ signaling domains.
ALLO-501A is generated by transfection of two pairs of TALEN mRNA: one pair to inactivate TRAC and one pair to inactive CD52 (Figure 4).
ALLO-501A is a pre-manufactured, TCRαβ depleted T cell suspension
The lentiviral vector used to generate ALLO-501A is derived from HIV-1
through the use of a third-generation vector, in which all sequences that encode lentiviral proteins have been deleted from the transfer vector.
The ALLO-501A dosage form is composed of CAR+_TCRαβ−_CD52+/− CAR T cells formulated at 20 × 106 viable CAR+ T cells/mL in a commercially available cryopreservation media.
All subjects will be treated with ALLO-501A 120 x 106 CAR+ cells following lymphodepletion.
